key_points: NVIDIA and CrowdStrike launched SafeMind, an agentic cybersecurity system built on NVIDIA Nemotron models.
The system operates in a continuous coevolution loop where offensive and defensive agents challenge each other.
CrowdStrike announced Falcon IQ to automate security workflows using more than 50 agents.
CrowdStrike reported that AI-enabled attacks increased by 89% in the past year.

items.summary: NVIDIA and CrowdStrike announced SafeMind, a new agentic cybersecurity system designed to counter automated attacks. Jensen Huang and George Kurtz stated that defense must evolve as quickly as offense. The system combines CrowdStrike's threat data with NVIDIA Nemotron models in a continuous coevolution loop. CrowdStrike also unveiled Falcon IQ to automate security workflows using over 50 agents. The companies tested SafeMind in a high-fidelity simulation of NVIDIA's infrastructure. Huang noted that AI-enabled attacks rose 89% in the past year. Kurtz emphasized that defenders now possess asymmetric advantages through this collaboration.
items.title: NVIDIA and CrowdStrike Announce SafeMind Agentic Cybersecurity System

The solution parses integration processes into structured formats to create detailed, version-controlled documentation without manual effort.
Boomi reports that the tool reduces documentation time by up to 85 percent while maintaining accuracy across thousands of customer processes.
The architecture utilizes Amazon Bedrock, Amazon SageMaker, and AWS Lambda to scale reliably for enterprise development teams.
items.summary: Boomi introduces Boomi Scribe, an AI-powered agent running on AWS that automates the creation and maintenance of technical documentation for complex enterprise integrations. The solution addresses the persistent technical debt caused by manual documentation efforts, which often lead to inconsistencies and compliance gaps. Boomi Scribe parses integration processes into Directed Acyclic Graphs and utilizes Amazon Bedrock and Claude models to generate accurate, user-friendly documentation automatically. The architecture leverages Amazon SageMaker for intent classification, Amazon S3 for storage, and AWS Lambda to orchestrate the pipeline across Boomi's 33,000 customers. By comparing version changes, the tool provides developers with concrete insights to improve planning and auditing. Boomi reports that the solution reduces time spent on documentation by up to 85 percent while ensuring accuracy across hundreds of daily processes.
items.title: Boomi Scribe automates documentation for enterprise workflows using AWS AI

items.summary: Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.1, which the company says sets a new standard for coding and long-running problem-solving tasks. A user tested the model's reasoning capabilities by generating SVGs of a pelican riding a bicycle at five different effort levels. The user then animated the max effort SVG for $1.37, noting minor wheel rotation artifacts in the video conversion. The article highlights how reasoning effort levels significantly impact output quality and cost.
items.title: Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.1 generates animated pelican SVGs

key_points: BenchMIRT analyzes individual prompts to disentangle mixed signals within LLM benchmarks.
The method identified that benchmarks like BBQ and WMDP correlate more with general reasoning than safety.
Keeping only 50% of questions in a benchmark often matches the full set's capability measure more closely.
The tool predicts model performance on unseen questions with 79% accuracy compared to 70% for simpler approaches.
items.summary: Researchers introduce BenchMIRT, a new method for auditing large language model benchmarks by analyzing individual prompts. The authors report that BenchMIRT applies multidimensional Item Response Theory to separate underlying capabilities like safety and general reasoning. The team trained the tool on results from 100 LLMs across 16 benchmarks and more than 34,000 questions. Analysis revealed that some benchmarks, such as BBQ and WMDP, align more strongly with general reasoning than their intended safety goals. BenchMIRT can also identify the most informative questions, predicting model performance on unseen items 79% of the time. The authors note limitations, including the use of models released by March 2025 and potential risks if informative questions are removed from evaluations.
items.title: Researchers introduce BenchMIRT to audit LLM benchmarks at the prompt level

key_points: Ai2 researchers introduce BenchMIRT to analyze individual prompts within LLM benchmarks.
The method separates mixed signals like safety and reasoning using multidimensional Item Response Theory.
Analysis of 100 models across 16 benchmarks showed some tests align more with reasoning than intended safety goals.
Keeping only 10% of benchmark questions preserved nearly the same model rankings as the full set.

items.summary: Ai2 researchers introduce BenchMIRT, a new method for auditing large language model benchmarks by analyzing individual prompts. The authors report that BenchMIRT applies multidimensional Item Response Theory to separate underlying capabilities like safety and general reasoning within single evaluations. Analysis of 100 models across 16 benchmarks revealed that some tests, such as BBQ and WMDP, align more strongly with reasoning than their intended safety goals. The tool also identifies the most informative questions, showing that keeping only 10% of items can preserve nearly the same model ranking as the full set. Ai2 states that BenchMIRT correctly predicted model performance on held-out questions 79% of the time, outperforming simpler approaches. The authors note limitations regarding models released after March 2025 and warn that question-level detail could allow unsafe models to pass trimmed evaluations.
items.title: Ai2 introduces BenchMIRT to audit LLM benchmarks at the prompt level

Companies differ in their approaches, with some retrofitting existing planes while others build from scratch, and varying strategies regarding AI usage and air traffic control communication.
items.title: Pyka and rivals race to deploy self-flying planes for cargo and farming

key_points: KIER scientists achieved a verified 26.7% efficiency for a small-area perovskite-CIGS tandem solar cell.
The result was confirmed by the Fraunhofer Institute and added to the US Department of Energy's efficiency chart.
Researchers developed specific interface materials to reduce light absorption and damage to the perovskite layer.
This new record surpasses the previous 26.3% efficiency held by KIST for cells under 1 cm².
items.summary: Scientists at the Korea Institute of Energy Research (KIER) reported achieving a world-record 26.7% efficiency for a sub-1 cm² perovskite-CIGS tandem solar cell. The result was verified by Germany's Fraunhofer Institute and included in the US Department of Energy's efficiency chart. Researchers stated they developed new interface materials to minimize performance losses during cell integration. Lead researcher In-Young Jeong noted the achievement improves both efficiency and stability. The previous record for this size category was 26.3%, set by KIST in July 2025.
items.title: KIER researchers achieve 26.7% efficiency for small perovskite-CIGS tandem solar cell

key_points: A new United Nations Environmental Programme report warns global temperatures will exceed the 1.5-degree Celsius threshold within a few years.
Scientists state the best chance for a safe climate requires immediate emission cuts, halving them by 2035, and removing billions of tons of carbon dioxide.
United Nations Secretary-General António Guterres called for accelerating the phaseout of fossil fuels and protecting climate allies like forests and oceans.
Climate researchers noted that recent extreme heat events show human systems are already overwhelmed by climate impacts at 1.4 degrees Celsius warming.
The report concludes that staying in the overshoot zone too long could push ice sheets and ocean currents past irreversible tipping points.
items.summary: Scientists warn that fossil fuel emissions are pushing Earth toward a dangerous climate overshoot phase where temperatures exceed the 1.5-degree Celsius Paris Agreement threshold within years. The United Nations Environmental Programme report states immediate cuts and carbon removal are essential to restore a safe climate. Experts say current warming rates could reach 2.7 to 3 degrees Celsius by 2100 without drastic measures. United Nations Secretary-General António Guterres emphasized the need to limit how high and long temperatures rise above the threshold. Researchers noted that recent extreme heat events in Europe and North America demonstrate that climate impacts are happening now, not in the distant future. The report highlights a critical gap between current adaptation capacities and the severity of upcoming climate-driven disasters.
items.title: UN Report Warns Climate Overshoot Imminent Without Immediate Action

items.title: NeoVolta secures 9 GWh of SK On cells for Georgia factory

items.summary: Jim Green, principal consultant and founder of Industrial Water Advisory, argues that power plants must evolve condenser chemistry management from reactive monitoring to predictive modeling. He details a three-stage progression in industry practices, moving from legacy indices like LSI to tagged chemistry, and finally to advanced digital twins. Green emphasizes that traditional grab samples and single-salt indices often fail to predict deposition accurately because they do not account for complex ion interactions at the tube wall. He reports that modern digital twins couple first-principles chemistry models with thermal-hydraulic simulations to calculate saturation ratios specifically at the hottest tube surfaces. According to Green, this shift allows operators to treat water chemistry as an optimization variable rather than a fixed compliance cost. He states that accurate modeling can forecast fouling rates based on intended chemical programs, enabling better decisions regarding cleaning intervals and cycles of concentration. Green warns that while tracers confirm chemical presence, they do not guarantee performance, and teams must validate models against historical plant data before trusting their outputs. He concludes that treating condenser chemistry as a performance lever yields significant economic benefits in heat rate and megawatt output.
items.title: Jim Green explains how predictive digital twins improve condenser chemistry management

items.summary: A new United Nations report states that global warming will likely exceed the 1.5°C target by 2030, a scenario Palau's President Surangel Whipps Jr described as unacceptable for Pacific Island nations. While the report indicates overshoot is probable, it notes that limiting peak warming to 1.8°C and subsequently using carbon removal methods could return temperatures to 1.5°C or below this century. Current global temperatures are already approximately 1.4°C warmer than pre-industrial levels, with extreme weather events intensifying worldwide. Experts warn that staying above 1.5°C risks triggering irreversible climate tipping points, such as the collapse of major ice sheets. Despite these challenges, the Paris Agreement has already averted an equivalent of 1°C of warming, keeping future temperatures on track for 2.6°C rather than 3.6°C. Future success depends on rapid emissions cuts, nature-based carbon removal, and international cooperation to protect vulnerable communities.
items.title: UN report says world will likely overshoot 1.5C climate target by 2030
